openQuestions: UI-05's diff overlay is computed client-side with a per-channel tolerance of 24 (web/src/compare.ts's CHANNEL_TOLERANCE) -- chosen empirically to absorb PNG re-encoding/anti-aliasing noise between two genuinely identical renders without being so loose it would hide a real one-pixel text change. Not derived from engine/verify.py's DEFAULT_TOLERANCE (0.001, a *fraction of pixels*, a different kind of threshold entirely) -- if the two ever need to agree exactly, that's a deliberate future alignment, not an oversight.

UI-05's 'before' image is always the document exactly as first opened (UndoRedoJournal.original_bytes), never 'the state before the most recent edit' -- i.e. comparing after two edits shows edit-1+edit-2 combined against the pristine original, not edit-2 in isolation. This matches SPEC.md 8.4's wording ('before/after split view', not 'per-edit diff' -- that's FNT-12, a different feature already built) and keeps the feature simple; a per-edit-in-isolation view was not attempted and would need journal.history's *individual* before/after snapshots exposed some other way.

UI-04's history panel shows only what was requested (an Op's own fields via journal.history/model_dump()), never the EditResult each op produced -- tier, confidence, verification are NOT part of GET .../history's response. SPEC.md's own mockup shows a richer per-edit summary ('14 hits, Exact') that this doesn't attempt; would need the journal itself to start recording results per entry, not just inputs. Documented in history.ts's module docstring, not a silent gap.

mypy --strict must be run scoped to `engine cli tools server` (matching .github/workflows' own `mypy engine cli tools server`), never over the whole tree -- running it over `tests/` too surfaces ~240 pre-existing errors (untyped PyMuPDF calls, missing generic type args) in test files that were never meant to be strictly typed and are not part of the actual CI gate. Learned by mistakenly running `mypy --strict .` in the UI-04 session and momentarily thinking something had regressed.

PyMuPDF's Document.tobytes() is NOT idempotent even with zero document changes between calls -- it regenerates a random component of the PDF's /ID array on every single call. Any future test (or feature) that compares to_bytes() output byte-for-byte across two calls, even on the exact same untouched Document object, will intermittently or deterministically fail for a reason that has nothing to do with actual content. Compare parsed content (get_text(), page_count, re-extracted spans, rendered PNG bytes) instead. This is now the second time this exact class of bug has been hit (previously: 'merely calling extract_font() perturbs serialization'; now: to_bytes() perturbs itself with no read in between at all) -- treat any new byte-identity assertion against PDF bytes (never PNG bytes, which render deterministically) as suspect on sight.

pip-audit in this sandbox flags CVEs in cryptography/httplib2/pip/pyjwt/setuptools/urllib3/wheel -- none are pdfworkerz's own dependencies (confirmed via grep against pyproject.toml; setuptools appears only as a build-system version floor). This is sandbox environment drift in the advisory database over time, not something a code change here introduces or can fix -- re-check whether this is still true (or has grown) at the start of the next session rather than assuming it's this session's fault.

UI-02's click-to-edit overlay approximates the font family/weight/style shown while editing (a name-based serif/sans/mono+bold/italic guess, src/overlay.ts) rather than loading the document's actual embedded font as a browser @font-face -- documented explicitly in web/README.md, not a silent gap. Size and color ARE exact (read straight from SpanStyle), and the actual committed edit goes through the same exact engine.edit pipeline as the CLI/server. Loading extracted font bytes as a web-font @font-face for pixel-accurate in-browser preview is a real, scoped-out future improvement, not attempted.

A real macOS-only CI failure was found and fixed after the UI-02/UI-03 push: two Playwright tests used Control+A to select all text before typing, which is 'move to start of line' on macOS (Cmd+A is select-all there), not select-all -- so typed text was inserted rather than replacing the original, only on the macOS shards. Fixed by deleting the keypress entirely rather than branching per platform: overlay.ts's startEdit() already calls selectAllContents() the instant a box becomes editable, so the six Control+A presses across these tests were always redundant, silently masked on Linux/Windows because those platforms treat Ctrl+A as select-all too. Lesson for any future Playwright test in this repo: don't reach for a keyboard shortcut to manipulate selection/focus state the app itself already establishes -- it's needless AND a cross-platform trap. Confirmed green on all three OSes at commit 3725ae5 (https://github.com/kalibudz/pdfworkerz/actions/runs/36365316425).

overlay.ts's cancelEdit() has a documented reentrancy fix worth reading before touching it: setting contentEditable=false on a focused element can synchronously fire blur, re-entering cancelEdit through box.onblur before the outer call finishes. Fixed by taking a local copy of the shared 'active box' reference and nulling the shared one immediately, before touching the box at all -- found via a real crash in the click-away test, root-caused by re-running against `vite dev`'s unminified source for a readable stack (the production build's minified stack was useless for finding it). Any future edit to this function's ordering needs to preserve that 'clear shared state before mutating anything' discipline.

ReplaceTextOp (search-based) must never be reused for a UI action that targets one specific span the user clicked -- it edits every occurrence of the matched text on the page, confirmed with a real two-identical-spans test. ReplaceSpanTextOp (index-based, via a fresh extract_page_spans + _span_at) is what click-to-edit uses instead; any future span-targeted UI action should follow the same index-based pattern, not text search.

PreviewTextOp/PageSpansOp are read-only and deliberately never journaled -- they're applied directly in server/app.py (like RenderPageOp and now render_original_page), not through the generic POST .../ops + journal.record path. A test (test_preview_route_never_appears_in_history) locks this in for PreviewTextOp. Any FUTURE read-only Op or route should follow the same direct-apply pattern, or it will pollute undo/redo history and clear the redo stack on every query.

viewer.ts's reloadDocument rebuilds the ENTIRE thumbnail rail (clears thumbButtons, calls buildThumbnailRail again) rather than invalidating just the current page's thumbnail -- simpler and correct, a deliberately accepted minor inefficiency (already-rendered thumbnails re-render) over adding a targeted per-thumbnail invalidation API. Worth revisiting only if edits become frequent enough for this to be a real perf issue.

First-ever green CI run: https://github.com/kalibudz/pdfworkerz/actions/runs/36356246278 (commit 9f68b0c, all 11 jobs). Local checks in this sandbox must go through `python3 -m <tool>` (mypy/ruff/pip_audit), not the bare commands on PATH, which resolve to unrelated tool installs here.

server/app.py's CORSMiddleware is scoped to a loopback-origin regex (127.0.0.1/localhost/::1, any port) -- deliberately permissive on port, reasoned through in the UI-01/06 session's PROGRESS.md entry: safe because auth here is a header a browser never auto-attaches, unlike a cookie. Revisit this reasoning before ever adding cookie-based or credentialed auth to this server.

web/package.json pins pdfjs-dist==6.3.289 deliberately: versions >=5.6.83 <6.2.108 carry a public high-severity CVE. npm audit is gated in CI's security job -- re-run it by hand after ever changing this pin.

web/src/polyfills.ts + web/src/pdf.worker.ts work around a real Map/WeakMap.prototype.getOrInsertComputed gap on an older browser engine (this sandbox's own pinned Playwright test browser). No-op on any browser that already has it natively.

tests/web/'s Playwright tests build on a *built* web/dist, never `vite dev` -- if web/dist doesn't exist, the whole module is skipped (not failed), so a plain `pytest` run with no prior `npm run build` silently produces no UI-0x evidence. CI always builds first; a human running tests locally needs to remember to.

fit=True (FNT-10) fragments a span's texttrace into one span per character, breaking a second edit's ability to find that text as one span -- defaults to False
FNT-09's kerning only reads legacy 'kern' tables, not GPOS pair positioning; no GSUB ligature substitution is attempted at all

font-name matching between texttrace and Page.get_fonts()/pikepdf goes through engine.fonts.match.normalize_font_name plus a containment-match fallback -- reuse this pattern rather than comparing font-name strings directly anywhere new

detect_blocks (engine/fonts/blocks.py) assumes its input span list is already in visual top-to-bottom order -- not guaranteed after an edit. Relevant if any future feature re-runs block detection on an already-edited page.

ReflowTextOp's overflow check runs before its require_tier check, so an overflowing edit is reported as overflow even when the font match is also weak -- both surface eventually with allow_overflow=True, but not in the most actionable order
